name: Sika Icosit KC 340/65
paste:
SIKA® ICOSIT® KC 340/65: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65, April 2026, Version 09.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/icosit-kc-340-65.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 09.01).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65 is a flexible 2-part polyurethane polymer resin grout that can be applied manually or by machine. It is designed as a vibration absorbing, load-bearing, flexible grout for fixing grooved or T–rails onto concrete slabs, steel bridge decks and tunnel invert slabs. Particularly suitable for embedded (floating) rail designs.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - As a noise and vibration reducing grout for continuous embedded grooved or T–rails and road crossing applications.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.11.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Two-part polyurethane grout for continuous embedded tracks with high axle loads
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2026, Version 09.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - DIN 45673-1: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive stiffness (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Heavy axle loads and standard deflection
    - Noise & vibration suppression
    - More uniform load distribution into substructure
    - Watertight undersealing
    - Flexible, elastic (shore A 70)
    - Damping, compressible
    - Good electrical insulation against stray currents
    - Excellent adhesion on various substrates
    - Levels out tolerances
    - Suitable as a powerful, shear-resistant adhesive
    - Absorbs dynamic stresses and prolongs the life of concrete substructure
    - Insensitive to moisture
    - Long durability, less maintenance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 2-part polyurethane
    - Colour: Grey
2.6 Density.
    | Part A | 0.9 kg/L |
    | Part B | 1.2 kg/L |
    | Part A + B | 0.9 kg/L |
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: 70 ± 5 (after 28 days); Shore hardness assists with material identification and assessing the curing progress on site. (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: 3.0 N/mm²
    - Tensile strain at break: 165 %
    - Electrical resistivity: ~5.48 × 10⁹ Ω·m
    - Service temperature: -40 °C minimum / +80 °C maximum short term +150 °C maximum
2.8 Chemical resistance. Long-term resistant against:
    - Water
    - Most detergents
    - Sea water
    - Mineral oils, diesel fuel
    - Organic solvents (ester, ketone , aromates) and alcohol
    - Concentrated acids and lyes
    Temporary resistant against:
    Short-term or no resistance against:
    Contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
2.9 Compressive stiffness. Static stiffness determined according to DIN 45673-1. Test specimen dimensions: 1000 x 180 x 25 mm (pure material value measured without rail); Preload: 1000 N; Testing speed: 2 kN/s; Maximum load: 50 kN; Bedding figure kstat = 192 [(kN/mm)/m] (±10 %)*, determined as per the secant method between 8 and 32 kN. *Deviation of the bedding figure and the curve are ±10 %.
2.10 System structure. System products:
    - Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65
    - Sikadur®-32+ for steel surfaces and green concrete
    - Sika® Primer-115 for steel surfaces and dry and matt damp mature concrete
    - Icosit® KC 330 Primer
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +10 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to packaging.
2.12 Packaging.
    | Manual application | Machine application |
    | Part A | 8.7 kg container | 160 kg drum |
    | Part B | 1.3 kg container | 24 kg container |
    | Part A + B | 10 kg | 184 kg |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 09.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Substrate must be sound, free from oil, grease, loose and friable particles. Slightly damp substrates are acceptable. Standing water must be removed (e.g. by vacuum extraction or oil free compressed air) before pouring Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65.
3.3 Substrate preparation. To improve adhesion, apply Icosit® KC 330 Primer as a primer on absorbent substrates (concrete). For corrosion protection, please contact local Sika technical service. Always comply with the waiting time limits between application of Icosit KC 330 Primer and pouring of Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65. Refer to the individual Product Data Sheets for more information.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2026, Version 09.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 100 : 15 (parts by weight)
    - Consumption: 0.9 kg per litre of volume to be sealed
    - Layer thickness: Minimum 15 mm; Maximum 60 mm
    - Pot Life: 8 minutes at +20 °C; After this time, the mixture becomes unusable. Higher temperatures will shorten pot life.
    - Curing time: Tack-free: 2 hours at +20 °C; Trafficable: 12 hours at +20 °C
4.3 Curing rate.
    | Shore A - Cur- | Curing rate at | Curing rate at | Curing rate at | Curing rate at |
    | ing Time | 0 °C | +5 °C | +23 °C | +35 °C |
    | 1 h | - | - | 30 | 35 |
    | 2 h | - | 20 | 40 | 45 |
    | 4 h | 20 | 30 | 45 | 50 |
    | 7 h | 35 | 40 | 50 | 55 |
    | 1 d | 55 | 55 | 60 | 65 |
    | 3 d | 60 | 60 | 65 | 65 |
    | 7 d | 65 | 65 | 65 | 65 |
    | 14 d | 70 | 65 | 65 | 65 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Waiting time to overcoating. Waiting time for applying the Product on primer or coating at +20 °C:
    | Product | Minimum | Maximum |
    | Icosit® KC 330 Primer | 1 hour | 3 days |
    | Sika® Primer-115 | 0.5 hour | 8 hours |
    | Sikadur®-32+ | 24 hours | 7 days |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Mixing.
    - The Product is supplied in pre-weighed composite units consisting of parts A + B.
    - Do not add any solvents to the Product.
4.6 Small packaging units. 1. Use an electric or pneumatic mixer with spiral or basket stirrer, diameter 120–140 mm, speed 600–800 rpm. 2. Stir Part A thoroughly until the material is completely homogeneous for at least 30 seconds in the original container. 3. Add Part B and mix for a further 60–80 seconds. Note Ensure the material from the container walls and the base is also mixed in. 4. During the final mixing stage, scrape down the sides and bottom of the mixing container with a flat or straight-edge trowel at least once to ensure complete mixing.
4.7 Big packaging units.
    - Large volumes of the Product can be mixed and applied with special two-part casting machines, which both mix and pump the material.
    - Large volumes of the Product can also be mixed using geared mixers, and application is performed separately. A suitable geared mixer is the GRS 300/1,5 from Geppert Rührtechnik GmbH, equipped with three blades Ø 300 mm. Refer to the equipment supplier’s instruction manual. Mount the agitator shaft on a drum lid which replaces the original lid during stirring. Stir Part A thoroughly, then add Part B and stir for approx. 5 minutes.
    Contact Sika Technical Services for information about suitable mixing machines.
4.8 Application. Material is suitable for application with special 2-part casting machines. Correct mix ratio must be carried out. Part A must be stirred at regular intervals. Reference must be made to equipment supplier’s instruction manual.
4.9 Application - Green and wet concrete.
    - Freshly applied Sikadur®-32+ with theoretical consumption: ~0.60 kg/m2 should be broadcasted with quartz sand, granulometry: ~0.2 up to ~0.8 mm, theoretical consumption: ~2 kg/m2.
    - 1) Concrete substrates: "green", the mat-damp concrete surface, after at least the first day of maturation, and on a min 14 days old concrete.
    - Substrate must be solid, rough and clean: the concrete surface should be free from loose fractions, dust, cement laitance, oil stains, grease and other contaminants. a) "Green", the mat-damp concrete surface, without a shiny layer of water on the surface (may be locally dry or mat-damp, with light and dark spots); should meet the following requirements, after at least the 1st day of maturing: the designed concrete class should be at least C30/37; the water/cement ratio of the designed concrete should be w/c= 0.50; the surface of fresh concrete should be "brushed" about 6-8 hours after mixing the concrete mixture with the use of stiff brushes in order to remove the cement laitance surface. b) Mature concrete substrate (min 14 days old): substrate strength tested using the "pull-off" method should be at least 1.5 MPa; concrete with no visible traces of moisture and no darkening caused by moisture. The concrete substrates must be prepared mechanically using suitable abrasive blast cleaning or planing / scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured gripping surface. High spots can be removed by grinding.
    - 2) Steel substrates must be prepared mechanically using suitable abrasive blast cleaning to remove all corrosion products and achieve a bright metal finish. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product and associated system products, preferably by vacuum extraction equipment.
    - Waiting Time / Overcoating: Minimum 24 hours, maximum 7 days
4.10 Cleaning of equipment. Mixing and application tools must be cleaned at regular intervals and immediately after use with Sika® Cleaner 5. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically
4.11 Limitations and important considerations.
    - To achieve the optimum flow performance, condition the material to a temperature of +15 °C before application.
    - Undersealing layer thickness must be a minimum 15 mm and maximum 60 mm.
    - To achieve maximum adhesion on concrete, loose particles and cement laitance must be removed mechanically, e.g. by blast cleaning or scabbling.
    - Use of appropriate Sika Primers will improve adhesion and durability.
    - Do not add any solvents to product.
    - Standing water must be removed before pouring.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. Condition product parts before application preferably at +15 °C to assist with flow and curing speed
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.4 Relative air humidity. 90 % max.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +35 °C max
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Dry to matt damp
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.11):
    - To achieve the optimum flow performance, condition the material to a temperature of +15 °C before application.
5.8 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Substrate must be solid, rough and clean: the concrete surface should be free from loose fractions, dust, cement laitance, oil stains, grease and other contaminants. a) "Green", the mat-damp concrete surface, without a shiny layer of water on the surface (may be locally dry or mat-damp, with light and dark spots); should meet the following requirements, after at least the 1st day of maturing: the designed concrete class should be at least C30/37; the water/cement ratio of the designed concrete should be w/c= 0.50; the surface of fresh concrete should be "brushed" about 6-8 hours after mixing the concrete mixture with the use of stiff brushes in order to remove the cement laitance surface. b) Mature concrete substrate (min 14 days old): substrate strength tested using the "pull-off" method should be at least 1.5 MPa; concrete with no visible traces of moisture and no darkening caused by moisture. The concrete substrates must be prepared mechanically using suitable abrasive blast cleaning or planing / scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured gripping surface. High spots can be removed by grinding.
5.9 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Shore A hardness: 70 ± 5 (after 28 days); Shore hardness assists with material identification and assessing the curing progress on site. (ISO 868)
5.10 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.11 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Icosit® KC 340/65, April 2026, Version 09.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/icosit-kc-340-65.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Icosit® KC 340/65 Part A, version 04/07/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sds-icosit-kc-34065parta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Icosit® KC 340/65 Part B, version 09/09/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/sds-icosit-kc-34065partb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
